source_text.body:
Generate lesson plans from a RAG library of past plans
An educator built a Claude project loaded with their old lesson plans in a RAG database, adding new material over time, and it now produces lesson plans for them.
·
Nov 16, 2026
Done with
CL
Claude
What they did
One teacher said they set up a Claude web project for lesson planning by loading it with favorite pre-AI lesson plans as a retrieval library, then kept adding new materials that worked well. They also attached a very detailed claude.md file with non-negotiables, alignment rules, rigor checks, discourse protocols, and authoring conventions so Claude would generate plans in that established style.
How it went
They said the project now produces great lesson plans for them. The thread gives no metrics or timing, and the main limitation implied is that quality depends on steadily feeding the project exemplars and detailed guidance.
Worth knowing
The key catch is the up-front work: the setup relied on a growing corpus of past plans plus a long custom claude.md specification.
Try it yourself
with
Claude
Copy prompt
I'm uploading my past lesson plans for [subject and grade level] to this project as reference material. Using their format, tone, and teaching style, write a new lesson plan on [topic] for [duration] that includes objectives, activities, materials, and an assessment. Finish with one complete plan, and then list which of my past plans you drew from so I can check it.
Original source: https://www.reddit.com/r/ClaudeAI/comments/1xxms7n/do_any_educators_use_claude_to_build_lesson_plans
